# Baseline and Agent Optimizer

## Establish the baseline

1. Define the task's quality measure, failure values, safety checks and
   acceptance policy before looking at optimized results. Use deterministic
   tests where meaningful, calibrated semantic/human evaluation where not.
2. Choose and label the baseline: a minimal vanilla model/tool policy, or the
   current production agent. Do not call an orchestrated, tuned agent
   "vanilla." Run it through the actual selected runtime.
3. Freeze code, instructions, tools, model/deployment/options, evaluator,
   external-state versions and price snapshot. Use group-disjoint search,
   training, development and final data; prevent label leakage into prompts
   and untrusted evidence from becoming a grading authority.
4. Agree on sample size/rollouts, concurrency and spending cap. Run the
   development evaluation adapter, retaining every planned episode.
5. Report the same quality, safety/protocol, latency and cost measures that
   will be used after optimization. Preserve raw outputs/tool traces and
   per-call usage. Use the cost tool after applying provider-specific cache
   normalization from the pricing reference.

Report completeness separately from quality. Infrastructure failures may
require a bounded repair, but never silently replace genuine model failures
with a successful resample. A changed environment or data version starts a
new run, not a continuation of old receipts.

## Configure the optimization search

Keep the model weights fixed. Identify the available knobs: system/developer
instructions, tool descriptions/schemas, skills, model settings, orchestration
limits, or other supported runtime configuration. Verify that the hosted
runtime actually reads the configuration generated by the optimizer.

Use optimizer-specific search data, not the sealed final test. Choose an
available optimization model and an evaluator supported by the current
service. Current optimizer documentation lists
[built-in and custom rubric evaluators](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/create-optimizer-dataset#customize-evaluators-advanced);
do not infer support for arbitrary code evaluators from ordinary evaluation APIs.
A built-in judge can nominate candidates without becoming the
project's final quality metric. Register or configure a custom evaluator
when required by the use case.

Discover current command syntax first:

```powershell
azd ai agent optimize --help
azd ai agent optimize status --help
azd ai agent optimize apply --help
azd ai agent optimize deploy --help
```

An inspected azd installation can submit using explicit values:

```powershell
azd ai agent optimize <agent-name> `
  --project-endpoint <project-endpoint> `
  --dataset <optimization-dataset> `
  --eval-model <evaluation-deployment> `
  --optimize-model <optimization-deployment> `
  --evaluator <supported-evaluator> `
  --max-candidates <approved-limit> `
  --no-wait --no-prompt
```

The command is billable. Approval and resolved values are prerequisites;
angle-bracket placeholders are not executable configuration. A service
configuration file is an alternative, but validate its current schema rather
than assuming old optimizer JSON/YAML fields remain supported.

Persist the returned run ID immediately. Monitor that run, not a new
submission; capture candidates and optimizer scores. If monitoring fails,
retrieve the existing operation before attempting any resubmission.
Inspect the underlying baseline evaluation early. Replay captured answers
through the canonical grader if valid answers receive zero; catalog response
bindings may contain serialized text-content blocks, not raw answer JSON.
An evaluation with zero outputs or repeated target-execution failures is an
infrastructure failure, not evidence of poor model quality. Stop the owned
job's retries before debugging or submitting a corrected search.

## Independently accept or reject

Materialize nominated candidates into isolated configuration directories or
new versions. Evaluate them on the same development cases and acceptance
metrics as the frozen baseline. Include usage from the full serving pipeline,
not merely the policy model's final call.

Choose improvements using the predetermined quality/safety/cost policy and
appropriate uncertainty analysis. Reject a higher optimizer-judge score
when project quality or required invariants regress. Approved efficiency
trade-offs must be explicit, not retrospectively called an accuracy win.

Record the retained configuration and measured deltas. Stop here if the goal
is met, RFT is unsupported, or evidence does not justify training.

Native candidate evaluation runs can use adaptive subsets. A run-local
`datasource_item_id` is not a stable dataset case identifier: match stored
case IDs or query/reference fingerprints, and report the actual coverage.
Do not zero-fill cases that the native run never scheduled or compare its
reported averages as though baseline and candidate had identical coverage.
Keep optimizer search evidence separate from a held-out serving comparison.
